name: Correlation — Host Exhibiting Multiple Distinct Attack Behaviors
description:
Attacker objective
Operate extensively on a single compromised host, leaving traces across several distinct attack techniques.

Attack logic
The more distinct high-fidelity techniques a single host exhibits in a short window, the higher the certainty of an active, hands-on-keyboard compromise rather than an isolated anomaly.

Why this detection works
Counting distinct high-fidelity JCB endpoint detections per host over the alert stream surfaces heavily-active hosts as a single, top-priority alert.

False positives
Very low — requires three independent high-fidelity detections on one host. A heavily-used administration host is the main candidate for tuning.

Tuning
Exclude verified administration hosts; lower or raise the distinct-detection threshold to fit the environment.

Required telemetry
The JCB Windows/AD detection alerts (host.name populated).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. host.name is the compromised endpoint; review the full list of distinct detections it produced.
2. Treat as a high-confidence active intrusion — isolate, preserve evidence and begin IR.
3. Reconstruct the timeline from the individual detections to scope the incident.
false_positives: Very low — requires three independent high-fidelity detections on one host. A heavily-used administration host is the main candidate for tuning.
query:
FROM .alerts-security.alerts-* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE host.name IS NOT NULL AND kibana.alert.rule.name IN ("Windows — LSASS Memory Dump via Known Credential-Theft Tooling", "Windows — Credential Theft: Registry Hive or NTDS.dit Extraction", "Windows — Malicious PowerShell: AMSI/ETW Bypass or Offensive Tooling", "Windows — Pass-the-Hash / Overpass-the-Hash Logon Pattern", "Windows — Ingress Tool Transfer via LOLBin", "Windows — Signed Binary Proxy Execution (LOLBin)", "Windows — UAC Bypass via Auto-Elevated LOLBin", "AD — DCSync: Directory Replication by an Unexpected Principal", "AD — Kerberoasting: RC4 Service Ticket Requested", "AD — AS-REP Roasting: TGT Requested for a Pre-Auth-Disabled Account", "AD — Shadow Credentials (msDS-KeyCredentialLink Modified)", "AD — SPN Added by Non-Computer Principal (Kerberoast Setup)", "AD — Domain Reconnaissance via LOLBins / BloodHound", "Windows — Remote Execution via WMI or WinRM", "Windows — Service Installed with Suspicious Image Path", "Windows — Inhibit System Recovery (Ransomware Precursor)", "Windows — Defender / EDR / Firewall Tampering", "Windows — Registry Persistence: IFEO / Winlogon / AppInit", "Windows — Scheduled Task Created with Suspicious Action", "AD — Member Added to a Privileged (Tier-0) Group", "AD — Object Security Descriptor Modified (DACL Backdoor)", "AD — Group Policy Object Modified by an Unexpected Principal", "AD — KRBTGT Account Password Reset (Golden Ticket Prep / Remediation)")
| STATS distinct_detections = COUNT_DISTINCT(kibana.alert.rule.name), detections = VALUES(kibana.alert.rule.name), alerts = COUNT() BY host.name
| WHERE distinct_detections >= 3
